subject: Governing law & injunctive relief — proposed compromise and runbook
messages:
From: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@apexcloud.com>

Cc: Apex Legal <legal@apexcloud.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines — governing law / emergency relief

Hi Soojin,

Attached are our markups to the MSA and order form. Main open items we need to resolve before SOC/IT sign-off: governing law (we prefer Delaware) and forum for provisional injunctive relief. Your redline retained broad arbitration and a mutual carve for emergency relief in any competent forum — that creates uncertainty for our procurement team.

Can Redwood accept Delaware law and an explicit forum for injunctive relief (they want SF Superior Court or, alternatively, a federal court in CA)? If not, we need clear fallback language that both sides can live with.

Attached: Apex_MSA_redlines_v2.docx (redline)

Thanks — want to get this to final before EOD Friday so procurement can queue POs.

— Olivia
Senior Counsel, ApexCloud

From: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-04-18T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — governing law / emergency relief

Olivia — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Monica (CS/Implementation) to weigh the commercial and operational impacts.

Two quick items from our side:
- Redwood prefers a clear arbitration pathway for disputes to avoid parallel proceedings.
- We also agree emergency/provisional relief should be available promptly; our ask is that either party be allowed to seek provisional injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve rights related to IP, data exfiltration, and live production outages.

Proposed options to move forward (we can pick one):
1) Governing law: Delaware. Dispute resolution: final disputes to arbitration (AAA/ICDR) in Delaware; carveout: either party may seek provisional injunctive relief in any competent court.
2) Governing law: Delaware. Dispute resolution: litigation in Delaware (exclusive forum) but with an expedited provisional relief process listed in the playbook (our preference if you cannot accept arbitration).

I've attached a short Emergency_Relief_Playbook (internal) which outlines SLOs, notice mechanics, escalation ladder and sample injunctive-relief language so your team can see how Redwood operationalizes a provisional relief carveout without creating indefinite forum exposure.

If you can confirm which option Apex prefers, Karthik will propose concrete clause language we can exchange.

- Soojin
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Emergency_Relief_Playbook.pdf (95KB)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@apexcloud.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-04-19T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — governing law / emergency relief (proposed clause)

Olivia — thanks, and thanks Soojin for the context. I reviewed Apex's redline and Soojin's options. Below is Redwood's proposed compromise language that we believe addresses Apex's commercial comfort while protecting Redwood's operational predictability:

(1) Governing law: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflicts of law principles.

(2) Dispute Resolution: Except for claims for provisional injunctive or other equitable relief, which either party may seek in any court of competent jurisdiction without prior submission to arbitration, the Parties agree to submit any remaining disputes to binding arbitration administered by the ICDR in Wilmington, Delaware. The arbitrator(s) shall apply Delaware law.

(3) Provisional Relief Mechanics: Either party seeking provisional injunctive relief shall: (a) notify the other party in writing of the specific emergency, (b) provide a reasonable opportunity to respond (unless delay would cause irreparable harm), and (c) seek relief in a court with subject matter and personal jurisdiction over the respondent. Any such provisional relief shall be deemed interim and without prejudice to the arbitrator's authority to determine the merits.

Rationale in brief:
- Arbitration preserves the streamlined remedy for most commercial disputes and is what Redwood uses to keep costs predictable.
- The injunctive carveout for any competent court gives Apex the speed and location flexibility it wants to address live-production or IP risks.

Attached is a marked-up clause draft (Redwood_proposed_injunctive_clause.docx) and a short note explaining enforceability considerations. If Apex can accept the carveout above, we can proceed to a single set of redlines and hand to procurement.

— Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_proposed_injunctive_clause.docx (6KB); Redline_summary_notes.txt (1.2KB)]

From: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@apexcloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Apex Legal <legal@apexcloud.com>
Date: 2028-04-20T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — governing law / emergency relief (Apex concurrence)

Karthik / Soojin — appreciate the clear framing and the playbook. After internal counsel review, Apex is willing to accept the arbitration pathway with the injunctive-relief carveout as drafted, subject to one narrow ask: because much of our operations and several key witnesses are in San Francisco, Apex requests that any provisional injunctive relief actions (where practicable) be brought in a California state or federal court sitting in San Francisco.

We understand that your compromise was to allow "any competent court," and we are fine with that language provided Redwood agrees to add a non-exclusive venue preference sentence: "Where practicable, the parties will consider forums located in San Francisco, California for interim injunctive relief." That will satisfy procurement and our business stakeholders.

If Redwood can accept that minor addition, we will update our mark and return a clean copy for signature and procurement can issue a PO the following week.

— Olivia
Senior Counsel, ApexCloud
